content_html_zh:
Consumer Agent Testing Tool (CATT) tests how an assistant uses your service. Run a scripted or model-driven agent against an MCP server, an MCP app, a website or an HTTP API. Check what the service did, inspect the evidence, and compare results across builds.

Muse and Instinct are supported surrogate emulation targets. Muse remains the default. Both use the shared connector testing contract, including routing, memory, payments, browser/HTTP tasks and scheduling. See the Instinct research for its sources and limits. The model that drives a trial is separate from the assistant being emulated.

Contributing | Security | Changelog | MIT license

A test host. CATT is a surrogate: it approximates an assistant's host, not its private implementation. A passing test does not certify compatibility with Muse or any hosted assistant. Each Muse-specific behavior has a recorded basis: documented, unofficial, assumed or unknown. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Meta, Instinct, OpenAI or Anthropic.

What you can test today

Lane 命令 它检查什么 现状和范围
MCP connectors connector-run SCENARIO Use the server's tools, apply account and approval rules, protect private values, and check the service's recorded outcome and the agent's answer. Muse and Instinct surrogates: --emulation-target muse|instinct. See connector lane.
Connector extensions connector-run SCENARIO with extensions: Routes, memory, custom API clients, browser actions, wallet cards, background jobs, untrusted content, channel limits and simulated users. Supported with the lane. user_simulator is exploratory and cannot run in scripted tests or decision contracts. See extensions.
Scenario scaffolding scaffold URL --output FILE, scaffold --from-run RUN --output FILE Read a tool catalog or turn an agent run into scripted calls. Calls no service tools. Replace every TODO(scaffold) before running. 支持。 One Streamable HTTP connector; no OpenAPI input.
Muse connector readiness check URL --suite muse-guidelines Review the catalog and optional manifest against the pinned connector guidelines without calling tools. Documented constraints, not admission. See readiness checks.
Shared surrogate readiness check URL --suite surrogate --emulation-target instinct Check the catalog, allowlist, schema syntax and selected projection without calling tools. CATT's contract for either target; see shared contract.
Personal Agent Protocol check ORIGIN --suite poppy Read poppy.json. With a manifest, probe sessions, sign-in and one declared operation on the company's hosts. Draft 0.1; no production Muse evidence.
Muse gadget registration check FILE --suite gadget Check a link.register message and command specs against the pinned SDK limits. Opens no connection. Documented limits, not admission. The SDK's terms say it is not a developer platform.
MCP protocol contracts check TARGET Check schemas, version negotiation, sessions and operation contracts; run the pinned conformance suite. 支持。 Generic MCP evidence; see readiness checks.
Embedded MCP apps surface-run SCENARIO Render the app in Chromium and check forms, tool calls, resources and service responses. An agent driver chooses from the scenario's scripted steps. 支持。 Generic MCP Apps host, not Muse. See host scope.
Websites browse POLICY, run --surface browser Act on accessibility snapshots under request rules. Takeover pauses the run (exit 3); the CLI has no handback. Native Chromium, without OS isolation. Browser scenarios use only the packaged reservation portal.
HTTP APIs run --surface api-tools, inspect, check Bind approval to each proposed call and check backend outcomes. Supported with a mapping. Your API also needs a loopback deployment and private control adapter. See API scenarios and API trials.
证据 report, export, replay, diff Inspect reports, redact exports, verify playback and compare runs. 支持。 Playback and diff require sealed runs.
Development extensions --development-extensions COMMAND CLI binaries, isolated browsers, cloud workers, local Glimmer, generated OpenAPI and Prism mocks. Outside the supported release. See development extensions.

The connector lane records the basis for each Muse-specific behavior. Tool classes and approval prompts follow documented guidelines. The muse-cli projection and template client follow unofficial mirrors; the native projection is an assumed generic baseline. The neutral cli projection supports both targets as a CATT treatment. Instinct runs have a separate source record and label the shared host algorithms as assumptions. Native/CLI MCP is CATT's test adapter; no public Instinct MCP integration contract was found.

Run the local booking example under Instinct without a model or account:

uv run consumer-agent-testing-tool connector-run examples/connector/instinct-booking.yaml \
  --driver scripted --script examples/connector/fixture-booking.calls.json \
  --start "python -m consumer_agent_testing_tool.connector_fixture --port {port} --variant good --auth none"

Set emulation_target: instinct in your scenario or pass --emulation-target instinct. Both targets use native or cli projection and the generic MCP client. Instinct defaults to plain-text replies and does not run Muse guideline checks. Its local wallet fixture covers payment behavior; live payment rails, trusted-network protocol, Vault and Files remain outside the shared contract.

Three quickstarts follow. The connector lane and the popular MCP server quickstarts run on loopback with no account; the Coverage Cat sandbox quickstart calls a hosted sandbox. Test your own service turns them into a workflow, and the documentation index lists every page.

Setup

You need Python 3.12 or newer (CI tests 3.12 on Linux and 3.14 on macOS), uv, and Node.js 20 or newer with npm (the installed packages declare >=20; tested with 25.9). The recorded release evidence covers macOS. From a clone of this repository, install the Python and Node dependencies and the Chromium build the browser lanes use:

uv sync --extra openrouter --extra dev
npm --prefix tooling ci --ignore-scripts
npm --prefix tooling/payment-ui ci --ignore-scripts
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.cache/ms-playwright" node tooling/payment-ui/node_modules/playwright/cli.js install chromium

The connector lane, the readiness checks and the scripted runs need only uv sync. Node and Chromium are for the MCP Apps and browser lanes.

On Linux (Debian or Ubuntu), install Chromium with its system libraries instead. Linux is not covered by the recorded release evidence: the commands below match the CI workflow but have not been qualified here.

sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nodejs npm   # or Node 20+ from nodesource or nvm
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv sync --extra openrouter --extra dev
npm --prefix tooling ci --ignore-scripts
npm --prefix tooling/payment-ui ci --ignore-scripts
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.cache/ms-playwright" \
  node tooling/payment-ui/node_modules/playwright/cli.js install --with-deps chromium

Three features rely on macOS Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) and report unsupported or blocked on Linux rather than running unconfined: the --offline readiness mode, the network-denied validator workers behind run --surface api-tools, and the local-model memory profile. The connector lane, the scripted runs, the readiness checks and the Docker-backed stdio targets do not depend on it.

Check the setup with doctor:

uv run consumer-agent-testing-tool doctor

It checks Node against the floors the installed packages declare, the tooling/payment-ui packages against their pinned versions, and Chromium and its headless shell under .cache/ms-playwright. It reports the optional protocol tooling, and checks Docker only for development lanes or configured stdio MCP and CLI targets. It makes no model requests, even when an existing configuration or --model-profile selects a model. Each failed or blocked check prints one line on stderr with its reason and, for a setup problem, the command that fixes it.

To explicitly run the provider preflight, which sends two short model requests and may incur charges, add --model-preflight:

uv run consumer-agent-testing-tool doctor --config agent.yaml --model-preflight

Scripted runs need no model account, and the scripted commands in all three quickstarts need no configuration file. Agent runs need a model profile and an API key; Model providers shows how to create one. Supply credentials through environment variables, and keep them out of scenarios and shared evidence. consumer-agent-testing-tool.yaml, the default settings file, is local and git-ignored, and no profile is shipped.

OpenRouter model and privacy settings

Consumer Agent Testing Tool requests zero data retention (ZDR) by default, even when routing.zdr is omitted. To change this, edit the selected profile in consumer-agent-testing-tool.yaml or the file passed to --config:

model_profiles:
  openrouter-dev:
    provider: openrouter
    api: chat-completions
    model_id: meta/muse-spark-open
    auth:
      mode: api_key
      env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
    routing:
      only: [together]
      allow_fallbacks: false
      require_parameters: true
      data_collection: deny
      zdr: true  # Set to false to disable this tool's per-request ZDR requirement.
defaults:
  model_profile: openrouter-dev

Use unquoted YAML booleans: true or false. Consumer Agent Testing Tool applies the setting to every OpenRouter request, including requests that continue after a tool result, and records it in the routing evidence.

Setting zdr: false removes this request-level requirement. It leaves data_collection: deny, the pinned provider and the ban on fallbacks in place. Your OpenRouter account or guardrails may still enforce ZDR. Request logs show the policy sent; they cannot independently verify the provider's retention practices. See OpenRouter's ZDR documentation.

Checked 15 October 2026: OpenRouter listed Together for Spark Open in both its model and ZDR endpoint catalogs. A live tool-call test passed with the routing settings above. Both responses identified Together, and the model used the tool result correctly. See the test record.

To choose another provider, set routing.only or pass --routing-provider to init. Requests never switch providers or models silently.

Runs use Inspect's dedicated openrouter provider, which replays earlier reasoning in structured form rather than as text. Each response must name the pinned provider. Responses do not name endpoint variants, so a pin such as nebius/fp4 is recorded as variant unverified. Streaming is not supported. See model providers.

With zdr: true, only ZDR-listed endpoints are eligible. On 15 October 2026, Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder were served only by Meta on OpenRouter and were not ZDR-listed, so no ZDR-compliant OpenRouter route existed for them. A request for them is expected to fail, but no live run has recorded the error. When OpenRouter's error cites the data policy, it is labeled no endpoint satisfies the routing/ZDR policy. With routing.only: [together], the init default, it may instead be labeled routing policy: no allowed provider.

Run a consumer test

This section covers the embedded MCP apps (surface-run), browser (browse) and HTTP API lanes. To let an agent use your MCP server's own tools, use the connector lane.

A scenario defines the endpoint, allowed origins, tools, private arguments, UI actions, consent requirements and result checks, and optionally an API key for the MCP connection (auth). Use endpoints and synthetic transactions you have permission to test.

consumer-agent-testing-tool surface-run path/to/scenario.yaml --driver scripted
consumer-agent-testing-tool surface-run path/to/scenario.yaml --driver agent --config agent.yaml
consumer-agent-testing-tool surface-run path/to/scenario.yaml --resume runs/existing-run
consumer-agent-testing-tool browse path/to/browser-policy.json --actions path/to/actions.json

The host declares MCP Apps support as a client, finds each tool's UI through its tools/list definition and renders it in a native browser. With --driver agent, the model picks among the scenario's steps (a scripted action menu) and never sees the server's tools, raw results or private inputs. Service checks determine the result; a rendered form or a model's claim of success cannot prove that a transaction completed.

browse drives a restricted browser through accessibility snapshots and element references, with no selectors, scripts or CDP. Its policy file sets the start url, the permitted origins and request rules, snapshot_max_chars (default 20,000), history_snapshots (2) and dialogs (agent, accept or dismiss), as in examples/browser-policy.json. Long snapshots are paged with {"kind": "snapshot", "offset": N}. Refused or failed actions come back to the agent as observations with a status, and dialogs and file choosers are answered with kind: dialog or kind: upload. With --driver agent, the provider preflight runs before the browser opens. The result's observations block counts truncated snapshots and refused actions. When the agent requests a takeover, the run pauses (exit 3). The CLI has no handback, so control does not return to the agent in that run. In native mode, WebSockets opened by dedicated workers and WebRTC TCP relays are not enforced. The policy field webmcp: true, off by default, lists page-registered WebMCP tools in the snapshot and lets the agent call them with kind: webmcp; that lane is labeled "generic WebMCP page tools, not Muse" (basis: assumed), and its evidence notes that Meta documents WebMCP for its AI glasses, a Meta product that is not Muse. See restricted browser behavior.

HTTP API tests use explicit mappings with the scenario runner. Mappings can send declared request headers and put the target credential in a custom API-key header. In API and browser trials, invalid tool proposals are returned to the model as tool errors, and exhausted limits fail the trial; see API scenarios. To test whether an agent can build its own client from an API's documentation instead, use the connector lane's custom_connector extension. Prism, Schemathesis and generated-OpenAPI tools are available only as development extensions. Their five packages with unresolved original license notices are excluded from the supported release, not treated as cleared.

Outcomes and exit codes

surface-run follows the exit codes in spec §18:

Exit 意义
0 完全的
1 Failed: an assertion, a service rejection, a UI interaction failure or an agent error
2 Setup, infrastructure, integration or reporting failure
3 Blocked or unsupported: waiting for a reply or approval, an unconfirmed write, a limit, or missing coverage

Before Surface report: ... it prints one line: Surface run <status> (exit N) at <stage> [<class>]: <reason>. result.json records the same failure_class and failure_stage, and whether the run is resumable. A completed run, or one that failed with exit 1, is final unless the failure left a write unconfirmed: that write may have taken effect, so the run stays resumable to reconcile it. Blocked runs and setup failures can resume.

run and browse use the same four codes, except that exhausting a turn, tool-call or time limit is a failure (exit 1). Only Inspect operator and custom limits, and in run a deadline that passed before an attempt's first generation, block instead (exit 3). run prints each evidence path on stdout. browse prints the final observation and its evidence path when the run completes or pauses for takeover, and nothing on stdout otherwise. For any outcome other than completed, both also print one line on stderr: <label> <status> (<class>) at <check>: <reason>. Evidence: <path>. The label names the step, for example Model preflight, Trial 2/10 of stale_total, Resumed trial of stale_total or Browse (doctor uses Doctor check). A run with a failed or blocked trial, or with --trials above 1, also prints a summary line with the counts. With --trials above 1 it adds the suite pass^k, the mean over scenarios, for example Run completed: 0 failed, 0 blocked and 4 completed of 4 trials; pass^1 1.00, pass^2 1.00. Evidence: .... The suite's metrics also break the trials down by scenario (statistical decisions). run DIR refuses (exit 2), before the preflight, a directory whose scenario files share an id.

connector-run prints the same stderr line, labeled for example Connector trial 1/1 of fixture-booking-happy-path; its codes are listed in the connector-lane quickstart. With --trials N, one code stands for all trials: 2 when any trial's evidence is not shareable, else 1 when any trial failed, else 2 when any hit a setup, harness or verification error, else 3 when any was blocked, else 0. The Connector trials: line on stderr gives pass^k and names the trials that are not shareable or ended in an error. The readiness suites' codes are in Readiness checks.

What the MCP Apps host implements

The embedded-app lane is generic MCP Apps host evidence (MCP Apps 2026-01-26), for hosts such as ChatGPT or Claude. It is not Muse evidence: Muse documents no third-party UI. Each result.json says so under mcp_apps_host.

The host implements:

  • the client capability (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui with text/html;profile=mcp-app), UI discovery from the tool's tools/list definition, and HTML resources as text or base64 blobs;
  • tool-input with the call's arguments, tool-result, and a hostContext (theme, display mode, locale, time zone, platform, container width and maximum height, and tool information);
  • a content security policy built from the resource's _meta.ui.csp, or the specification's restrictive default when the resource declares none, and the declared camera, microphone, geolocation and clipboard-write permissions;
  • in the native renderer, a sandbox proxy on an origin separate from the host page. With browser_origins, the host page also has Chromium's local-network-access permission, every redirect hop is checked again (GET or HEAD to an allowlisted origin only), and each direct write is recorded as an unconsented host_action before it is sent;
  • view tools/call requests for the step's allowlisted tools, and resources/read and resources/list for the step's callback_resources;
  • ui/message, delivered once to agent runs in the next observation a model reads, as app_messages; the view is told when the host does not deliver it. ui/update-model-context, ui/open-link, display-mode, log and teardown requests are recorded, and the latest model-context update reaches agent runs as app_context;
  • size changes, ui/resource-teardown before the view closes, and tool-cancelled when the view never received the call's result;
  • _meta.ui.visibility, for view calls and for tool steps;
  • MCP 2026-07-28 servers, when the scenario sets version_negotiation: auto. The default is the 2025 initialize handshake;
  • an API key on the MCP connection (auth), as a bearer token, a custom header or a query parameter;
  • a legacy window.openai bridge.

It does not implement a model turn for a view's message, resource templates, _meta.ui.domain, display modes other than inline, partial tool input, host-context change notifications, OAuth on the MCP connection, or consent for a view's direct writes in the native renderer. The legacy bridge and the isolated renderer have no sandbox proxy. See MCP Apps host.

Inspect retained evidence

consumer-agent-testing-tool report runs/existing-run
consumer-agent-testing-tool export runs/existing-run
consumer-agent-testing-tool replay runs/existing-run
consumer-agent-testing-tool diff runs/baseline runs/candidate

Replay checks the evidence seals and stops on a mismatch. It never substitutes a live request. To test the service again, start a new run. Reports mark missing measurements as unknown and keep partial totals distinct from complete totals.

Reports open with the verdict, which names the failing step and check, then the checks and host capabilities, and a per-step timeline that shows what the model received in full. Then come a connectors table for runs with several connectors, the surface views (what the service published, what the model was offered, what it received at each step, and what only the developer sees), the metrics, and the viewers and linked evidence: agent and preflight runs, their Inspect logs and the inspect view command, and, locally, a captured Playwright trace. Gaps and limits follow, then the run lock and the full recorded result, each collapsed; see report layout. report on an agent sub-run of a sealed run returns its sealed report unchanged.

Evidence files and exports hide credentials, registered secrets, contact details and other personal fields such as names and addresses. Model views keep the user's own data visible: they hide only credentials and declared secrets, plus browser password fields and, in a resumed browser scenario, text typed in an earlier attempt. The provider boundary refuses any model request that still contains a registered credential. Export also applies the run's own private values, which are never exported, and refuses (exit 2) when a staged file, or a member of an Inspect log or other archive, still holds one. See redaction.

diff compares two sealed runs, such as surface, browser or connector runs. A change to the package source counts as a run-lock change, so compare runs made from the same checkout. It exits 0 when they are comparable with no outcome regression, and 1 when an outcome regressed: a worse status, or a passing check that no longer passes or is missing. It exits 3 when they are not comparable, because of a run-lock change outside --treatment or an unsealed or unverifiable run. Generated IDs and service timestamps are normalized; run locks are compared exactly. --ignore POINTER (repeatable) excludes a JSON pointer under /outcomes, /capabilities or /milestones, and --treatment /server declares an intentional server build change. See replay and diff.

Use it in CI

Scripted connector runs need no model and no key, and they replay the same calls every time, so they work as a pull-request check. connector-run can start the service itself and write reports a CI system reads:

uv run consumer-agent-testing-tool connector-run my-connector.yaml \
  --driver scripted --script my-connector.calls.json \
  --start "python -m my_service --port {port}" \
  --junit reports/connector.xml --summary-json reports/connector.json
  • --start COMMAND runs the service on a free loopback port. The command is split like a shell command but not run in a shell. {port} in the command is that port. The service also gets it as PORT and the scenario as ${PORT}. The tool waits until --ready-url, or the scenario's first connector endpoint, answers HTTP. It waits at most --ready-timeout seconds (default 30). When the run ends, the service's process group gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 seconds. Its output goes to runs/service-<id>.log, outside the sealed run. That log isn't redacted, so pass secrets to the service through the environment. The run lock records the command with credentials redacted. A service that exits early or never becomes ready exits 2.
  • --junit FILE writes one test suite per trial and one test case per check. Blocked checks are <skipped>. check --suite muse-guidelines accepts it too.
  • --summary-json FILE writes the verdict, exit code, checks, trials, pass^k and run paths. Its format is schemas/summary-v1.schema.json. --summary-json - prints only that JSON on stdout and moves the other lines to stderr.
  • Both reports are also written when the command stops with an error. See CI outputs and services.

The exit codes in Outcomes and exit codes decide the step. A 3 (blocked or unsupported) is not a pass. examples/ci/connector-lane.yml is a GitHub Actions template with two jobs. On pull requests, it runs the scripted calls and the readiness review. Nightly or on demand, it runs agent trials under each Muse-like treatment, and only when a model key secret is set. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs this repository's tests and shipped examples on macOS and Linux. Coding agents should start with AGENTS.md. All matrix jobs feed the required CI check; Linux failures are not allowed to pass silently. Workflow validation, tracked-file hygiene, secret scanning and schema freshness are checked too.

Running the tests

Plain pytest runs the supported collection:

uv run pytest -q

tests/conftest.py gives each session a temporary directory, home and cache under .cache/pytest/, removes them after a passing session, and removes the surface and browser run directories its tests create under runs/. The full collection takes about twenty minutes and makes no network request beyond loopback and no model request. pytest --development-extensions also collects the experimental tests, which may need other runtimes, tools and external evidence. Async cleanup and unhandled thread exceptions fail tests instead of remaining warnings. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the review workflow and the launch checklist for the private-to-public transition.

Release audit

The supported release is local-consumer-v1: the connector lane and its extensions, the readiness checks, consumer MCP apps, the restricted browser, mapped HTTP APIs, transactional consent, continuation, evidence and replay, measurements, the distribution, and the OpenRouter and Meta Model API adapters. Real-Muse calibration, cloud provisioning, local Glimmer, browser OS isolation and live Bedrock qualification are outside it; see release scope for the full boundary.

Release evidence is generated per release and is not committed. docs/release-gates.json is the committed policy: the gates, the scope and the exclusions. The release workflow runs on a v* tag. It records every gate on macOS, requires the audit to pass, and attaches three things to the GitHub release:

  • the wheel and the source archive, with signed build provenance;
  • release-evidence-<commit>.tar.gz, which holds release/release-gates.json (the recorded ledger) and release/evidence/.

Use consumer-agent-testing-tool release-audit to check release readiness. It reads release/release-gates.json when evidence has been recorded or extracted there. Without it, it reads the committed policy and reports every gate unverified. Exit code 0 means release-ready for local-consumer-v1; exit code 3 means at least one required gate needs attention. The evidence binds a digest of the source, so a source change or an expired gate (seven days after recording) cannot inherit an earlier passing result. To audit a published release, check out its tag, extract its evidence archive at the repository root and run the audit before the gates expire.

Day to day, you don't need any of this. Run the tests for what you change, and let CI run the full collection on each pull request.

A separate live Spark Open test passed through Together with ZDR enabled. It verified native tool calls, continuation after a tool result, and the requested routing policy. It did not test streaming, independently verify retention practices, or establish compatibility with every consumer workflow. The Coverage Cat checkout failure described above remains an open integration issue.

The audit requires five gates:

Gate Evidence required
Regression Every test in the default supported collection passes, with no skips
分配 Fresh offline installation, original dependency notices, artifact integrity and packaged consumer workflows
Transactional consent Passing consent, continuation and effect checks in the current regression
Replay/diff Passing evidence-integrity and comparison checks in the current regression
Surrogate parity Exact Muse/Instinct native/CLI cases, memory lifecycle, routing, payment, readiness and extension coverage

To record evidence locally instead, for example before tagging, run the same steps as the workflow, in this order. verify_distribution.py regenerates the dependency notices, which are part of the source fingerprint, so the distribution comes before the regression. The regression takes about twenty minutes. Everything is written under release/, which git ignores:

.venv/bin/python scripts/verify_distribution.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/record_distribution.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/run_regression.py release/evidence/regression-run.xml
.venv/bin/python scripts/record_regression.py release/evidence/regression-run.xml
.venv/bin/python scripts/record_release_tests.py release/evidence/regression-run.xml
consumer-agent-testing-tool release-audit

run_regression.py refuses an existing report path, so remove release/ or pick a new name to record again. It records workspace-relative paths and writes the home directory as ~ in the log.

Distribution checks use caches in the workspace and the installed browser. They need no Docker VM, cloud worker or model credentials. If a dependency cache is missing, populate it separately with scripts/verify_distribution.py --prepare-cache; that setup step uses the network. The installation evidence covers macOS only.

The audit verifies source fingerprints, artifact hashes, required checks and expiry dates. It returns 0 when every required gate passes, or 3 otherwise. Excluded capabilities remain labelled as excluded. Qualification inputs explains what each gate needs.

Development extensions

The repository retains worker, isolation, local-model, calibration and generated-OpenAPI experiments, and the CLI/skill lane for a developer's own CLI binary (run --surface cli-skill), which needs Docker and an oracle that returns the reservation fixture's snapshot schema. The normal CLI rejects these paths. To use them, put --development-extensions before the subcommand and install the separate development-extensions dependency group and any required tooling. These experiments are outside the supported release. The supported way to give an agent a CLI over an MCP server is connector-run --projection muse-cli.

The optional Node API tools have known dependency advisories. Do not use them with untrusted inputs while those findings remain open.
